messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 22k error-429 spikes in inference-gateway-prod across 3 regions (severity: high) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: links: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/4221 · runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/inference-429
ema (oncall): I’m on it. I’m shifting pages to me. @liam do you have bandwidth to look at grouping/dedupe while I confirm customer impact?
liam (sre): Yep, I can take grouping. Initial look — alerts are primarily from short bursts of retries from SDK clients hitting burst limits. Lots of nearly-identical request IDs.
zoe (prod-eng): seeing related error patterns in our logs: `prefix_kv_cache_miss -> 429` followed by rapid retries. Could be an SDK backoff regression in 0.9.3.
noah (support): I’m checking open tickets — two customers reported degraded burst responses, not full outage. One is a paid enterprise with real-time use.
ema (oncall): Customer impact: partial degradation for some high-throughput sessions, not full outage. Prioritize mitigation to reduce PD noise, then fix SDK.
liam (sre): Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily raise dedupe window for the 429 alert from 3s -> 30s; 2) Group alerts by `client_app_id` + `region` instead of full request hash; 3) Add a short-lived rate cap on alerting for this rule (max 5 notifications / 10min). Thoughts?
ema (oncall): +1. Start with grouping and rate cap. I’ll create a temp squelch if PD starts paging repeatedly.
zoe (prod-eng): We can also flip a feature-flag in the SDK rollout to enable exponential backoff for 2xx/429 paths — but that’s a code change (next deploy). For immediate, grouping/rate cap is faster.
liam (sre): Doing commands now:
```
# update alert rule
PUT /api/alerts/4221
{
  "group_by": ["client_app_id","region"],
  "dedupe_window_secs": 30,
  "rate_limit": {"max_pages": 5, "per_seconds": 600}
}
```
liam (sre): applied. Dashboard notifications show grouping keys collapsed. PD flurry should drop.
incident-bot: Action: alert rule 4221 updated by liam.
noah (support): Noted. I’ll ping the enterprise contact and confirm they see improvements, also mention a correlation with SDK version.
ema (oncall): I’m enabling a 15m temporary PD squelch for the rule to avoid cascading pages while we observe. If we still have customer impact, we’ll escalate.
```
# squelch command (internal)
POST /api/oncall/squelch
{
  "alert_id": 4221,
  "duration_mins": 15,
  "reason": "burst retry storm, temporary squelch while grouping and rate limit applied"
}
```
incident-bot: Squelch active for alert 4221 until +15m.
liam (sre): After grouping, # of active pages dropped from ~420 -> 18 (last 5m). Graph: https://dash.redwood.ai/graphs/4221/grouping-experiment
zoe (prod-eng): Nice. Logs also show fewer retry loops after some clients respected new server-side throttling.
ema (oncall): Good short-term win. Let’s capture follow-ups:
- create ticket to revert dedupe_window back when SDK fix ships (or to set to 10s as compromise)
- prod-eng to ship SDK backoff fix (zoe)
- monitoring: add a per-client 429 rate metric and a dashboard tile for quick triage (liam)
- docs: add runbook step for temporary squelch + grouping change (noah)
liam (sre): Creating follow-up ticket: PROD-3245 — "Investigate 429 bursts: SDK backoff + alerting tuning". Assigning to zoe + liam. ETA: EOD tomorrow for triage notes.
zoe (prod-eng): I’ll prioritize a quick patch to the SDK to enable jittered exponential backoff and a guard that prevents immediate retry loops. Will open PR and request expedited review.
noah (support): I contacted the enterprise customer — they confirm less noisy retries and fewer degraded sessions. They appreciated the heads-up.
ema (oncall): Great. For monitoring/dashboards: liam, can you add a heatmap of 429s by `client_app_id` over the last 24h and a small alert that fires only when a single client exceeds 1k 429s in 10m? That will reduce multi-tenant noise.
liam (sre): Will do. Proposed PromQL for the tile: `sum by (client_app_id) (increase(inference_gateway_429_total[10m]))` and alert when > 1000. I’ll add as a non-pager alert at first (slack-only), then escalate if needed.
ema (oncall): Add it as slack-only initially. Also add a dashboard panel with a top-10 client table.
liam (sre): Added panel + slack-only alert. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/429-heatmap
zoe (prod-eng): Once SDK PR is open I’ll tag QA and get a hotfix out. We should also plan to revert the long dedupe window after SDK is rolled out; otherwise we hide sharp regressions.
noah (support): I’ll update the customer-facing incident note: brief summary + mitigations + ETA for SDK fix.
ema (oncall): Thanks team. I’m closing this live thread in 20m if no further regressions. Action items summary (ema):
- liam: prod ticket + dashboard + slack-only alert (PROD-3245 comment)
- zoe: open SDK PR + expedited review
- noah: customer comms + runbook doc update
- ema: revert squelch and audit alert noise after 15m window
liam (sre): Noted. Recording the experiment parameters in the ticket (dedupe 30s, grouping client_app_id+region, rate cap 5/10m, squelch 15m).
incident-bot: Incident thread closed by ema (oncall) after 18m. Final status: mitigated for paging; customer impact limited.
ema (oncall): Follow-up — we should run a small experiment next week with a conservative dedupe baseline (10s) and a tighter grouping key to avoid blinding signal for one-off regressions. Schedule a short postmortem sync. :calendar:
zoe (prod-eng): Agreed. I’ll add RFC notes to the ticket about long-term monitoring improvements.
noah (support): Thanks all. I’ll paste the customer note into the ticket and Slack channel after this thread. :white_check_mark:
